Baranyi and Yam proposed the concept of '''[[HOSVD| M-mode SVD/HOSVD]]-based  [[canonical form]]''' of TP functions and quasi-LPV system models.<ref name=canon1>{{cite conference
|author =       P. Baranyi and L. Szeidl and P. Várlaki and Y. Yam
|title =        Definition of the HOSVD-based canonical form of polytopic dynamic models
|book-title =    3rd International Conference on Mechatronics (ICM 2006)
|date =         July 3–5, 2006
|pages =        660–665
|place =      Budapest, Hungary
}}</ref><ref name=ykc00>{{cite book
|author = P. Baranyi, Y. Yam and P. Várlaki
|title = Tensor Product model transformation in polytopic model-based control
|publisher= Taylor & Francis |location=Boca Raton FL
|year = 2013
|page = 240
|isbn = 978-1-43-981816-9 <!--(IN PRINT)-->
}}</ref> Szeidl et al.<ref name=canon3>{{cite journal
|author =       L. Szeidl and P. Várlaki
|title =        HOSVD Based Canonical Form for Polytopic Models of Dynamic Systems
|journal =      Journal of Advanced Computational Intelligence and Intelligent Informatics
|year =         2009
|volume =       13
|number =       1
|pages =        52–60
|doi = 10.20965/jaciii.2009.p0052
|doi-access =free
}}</ref> proved that the [[TP model transformation]]<ref name=Baranyi04>{{cite journal
|author =       P. Baranyi
|title =        TP model transformation as a way to LMI based controller design
|journal =      IEEE Transactions on Industrial Electronics
|date=April 2004
|volume =       51
|number =       2
|pages =        387&ndash;400
|doi=10.1109/tie.2003.822037
|s2cid = 7957799
}}</ref><ref name=compind>{{cite journal
|author =       P. Baranyi and D. Tikk and Y. Yam and R. J. Patton
|title =        From Differential Equations to PDC Controller Design via Numerical Transformation
|journal =      Computers in Industry
|year =         2003
|volume =       51
|issue = 3
|pages =        281&ndash;297
|doi=10.1016/s0166-3615(03)00058-7
}}</ref> is capable of numerically reconstructing this canonical form.  

Baranyi and Yam employed the ideas described by De Lathauwer ''etal''<ref name="DeLathauwer00">{{Cite journal|last1=De Lathauwer|first1=L.|last2=De Moor|first2=B.|last3=Vandewalle|first3=J.|date=2000-01-01|title=A Multilinear Singular Value Decomposition|journal=SIAM Journal on Matrix Analysis and Applications|volume=21|issue=4|pages=1253–1278|doi=10.1137/s0895479896305696|issn=0895-4798}}</ref> and the algorithm developed by Vasilescu and Terzopoulos under the name [[HOSVD|'''M-mode SVD''']].<ref name=":Vasilescu2002">{{cite conference
|author=M. A. O. Vasilescu, D. Terzopoulos
|title=Multilinear Analysis of Image Ensembles: TensorFaces 
|book-title=Proc. 7th European Conference on Computer Vision (ECCV'02) 
|location=Copenhagen, Denmark
|year=2002
|url= https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?repid=rep1&type=pdf&doi=67eb22ae0baf86af77188fc0ab27edacf07a9140}}</ref><ref name=":Vasilescu2005">{{cite conference
|author=M. A. O. Vasilescu, D. Terzopoulos
|title=Multilinear Independent Component Analysis
|book-title=Proc. IEEE Conf. on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR'05) 
|location=San Diego, CA
|year=2005}}</ref> The M-mode SVD is referred in the literature as either the '''Tucker''' or the [[HOSVD]]. The Tucker algorithm and the DeLathauwer ''etal.'' companion algorithm<ref name=":2">{{Cite journal|last1=De Lathauwer|first1=L.|last2=De Moor|first2=B.|last3=Vandewalle|first3=J.|date=2000-01-01|title=On the Best Rank-1 and Rank-(R1 ,R2 ,. . .,RN) Approximation of Higher-Order Tensors|journal=SIAM Journal on Matrix Analysis and Applications|volume=21|issue=4|pages=1324–1342|doi=10.1137/S0895479898346995|issn=0895-4798}}</ref> are [[sequential algorithm]] that employ [[gradient descent]] or the [[Power iteration|power method]], respectively.

Related definitions (on TP functions, finite element TP functions, and TP models) can be found [[TP model transformation|here]]. Details on the control theoretical background (i.e., the TP type polytopic Linear Parameter-Varying state-space model) can be found [[TP model transformation in control theories|here]].

A free [[MATLAB]] implementation of the TP model transformation can be downloaded at [https://web.archive.org/web/20120229061018/http://tptool.sztaki.hu/] or at MATLAB Central [http://www.mathworks.com/matlabcentral/fileexchange/25514-tp-tool].

==Existence of the M-mode SVD/HOSVD canonical form==

Assume a given finite element TP function:

:<math>f(\mathbf{x})=\mathcal{S}\boxtimes_{n=1}^N \mathbf{w}_n(x_n),</math>

where <math>\mathbf{x}\in \Omega \subset R^N</math>. Assume that, the weighting functions in <math>\mathbf{w}_n(x_n)</math> are othonormal (or we transform to) for <math>n=1,\ldots, N</math>. Then, the execution of the HOSVD on the core tensor <math>\mathcal{S}</math> leads to:

:<math>\mathcal{S}=\mathcal{A}\boxtimes_{n=1}^N \mathbf{U}_n.</math>

Then,

:<math>f(\mathbf{x})=\mathcal{S}\boxtimes_{n=1}^N \mathbf{w}_n(x_n) = \left(\mathcal{A}\boxtimes_{n=1}^N \mathbf{U}_n\right) \boxtimes_{n=1}^N \mathbf{w}_n(x_n),</math>

that is:

:<math>f(\mathbf{x})=\mathcal{A}\boxtimes_{n=1}^N \left( \mathbf{w}_n(x_n) \mathbf{U}_n\right) = \mathcal{A}\boxtimes_{n=1}^N \mathbf{w'}_n(x_n),</math>

where weighting functions of <math>\mathbf{w'}_n(x_n),</math> are orthonormed (as both the <math>\mathbf{w}_n(x_n)</math> and <math>\mathbf{U}_n</math> where orthonormed) and core tensor <math>\mathcal{A}</math> contains the higher-order singular values.

==Definition==

;HOSVD (M-moe SVD) canonical form of TP function

::<math>f(\mathbf{x})=\mathcal{A}\boxtimes_{n=1}^N \mathbf{w}_n(x_n),</math>

* Singular functions of <math>f(\mathbf{x})</math>: The weighting functions <math>w_{n,i_n}(x_n)</math>, <math>i_n=1,\ldots,r_n</math> (termed as the <math>i_n</math>-th singular function on the <math>n</math>-th dimension, <math>n=1,\ldots,N</math>) in vector <math>\mathbf{w}_n(x_n)</math> form an orthonormal set:
::<math>\forall n:\int_{a_{n}}^{b_{n}}\tilde{w}_{n,i}(p_{n})\tilde{w}_{n,j}(p_{n}) \, dp_n=\delta_{i,j},\quad1\leq i,j\leq I_n,</math>
:where <math>\delta_{i,j}</math> is the [[Kronecker delta]] function (<math>\delta_{ij}=1</math>, if <math>i=j</math> and <math>\delta_{ij}=0</math>, if <math>i\neq j</math>).
* The subtensors <math>{\mathcal{A}}_{i_n = i}</math> have the properties of
** all-orthogonality: two sub tensors <math>{\mathcal{A}}_{i_{n}=i}</math> and <math>{\mathcal{A}}_{i_{n}=j}</math> are orthogonal for all possible values of <math>n,i</math> and <math>j:\left\langle
{\mathcal{A}}_{i_{n}=i},{\mathcal{A}}_{i_{n}=j}\right\rangle
=0</math> when <math>i\neq j</math>,
&* ordering: <math>\left\|
{\mathcal{A}}_{i_n=1}\right\| \geq\left\|
{\mathcal{A}}_{i_n=2}\right\|  \geq\cdots\geq\left\|
{\mathcal{A}}_{i_n=r_n}\right\|  >0</math> for all possible values of <math>n=1,\ldots,N+2</math>.
* <math>n</math>-mode singular values of <math>f(\mathbf{x})</math>: The Frobenius-norm <math>\left\|
{\mathcal{A}}_{i_n=i}\right\|  </math>, symbolized by <math>\sigma_i^{(n)}</math>, are <math>n</math>-mode singular values of <math>\mathcal{A}</math> and, hence, the given TP function.
* <math>{\mathcal{A}}</math> is termed core tensor.
* The <math>n</math>-mode rank of <math>f(\mathbf{x})</math>: The rank in dimension <math>n</math> denoted by <math>rank_n(f(\mathbf{x}))</math> equals the number of non-zero singular values in dimension <math>n</math>.
